scores.why: Unmistakably phosphor with real glow, but near-monochrome, flat and loosely typeset; the owner has said it needs variation and structure, and there is no line language.

The Grid Console carries the owner's favourite thing, fine tracks with nodes, a NOW node and lit rails, through every page (Home, To do, Plans, Status, Settings), with bright green kept for the key word, the monitors and the primary key. The calmer lattice lowers glare and the grounded steel, amber and violet companions stay low-chroma. Differences from its parent are quiet, but the parent was already the strongest system.

The same console with the hatched plates and corner ticks, which give it the most texture and the strongest machine feel. The page is busier and the lattice slightly shouts, which is the one thing Calmer fixes. Still very much a phosphor console on every page.

A bold restructure with a real CRT tube holding a bar-chart scope, a Contents plate, and fine lit rails on the To do rows. It is the most different from today and keeps the glow, but it is dense. The columns on Home are uneven and the left rail on Status and Plans is heavy, so it reads more like an instrument panel than a family page.

Slate Track Diagram with a rail from Vera's screen to the question box and 'was due N days ago' stamps, so it has good line language and a clear voice in the content. The serif headings are tasteful, but the big glowing Add key bar on To do is glare, and the page is closer to today's layout than the others.

The same track-diagram system without the rolled changes: good rails on Chat and To do, scanlined key word, and a serif and slate look that is calmer. It is a little plainer than Rail Keys and has no head-to-box rail.
placeholder

The editorial condensed type and giant lit MIND are striking, and the chat rail is a good addition. But the line language stops at rules and one thread, Status/Plans/Settings read as stark typographic pages, and the phosphor character lives mostly in the tubes and the one word.

The parent of the cool-rail variant: strong typesetting and a dramatic Home, but cream and brass warmth drift from the owner's cool, CRT-leaning taste and it has no tracks, so it loses the line art the owner values.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the tracks, NOW node and 44px targets. Bring back a restrained version of the hatched blank plate or a single lit corner tick on the focused cell only, so the console identity is not lost. Make the half-size difference from its parent more visible, for example through slightly stronger kind colours in the cell labels.
Keep the hatched plates and ticks but soften their outlines; the page gains from texture but needs a quieter lattice, which is Calmer's change. Check the very busy Chat page grid foot.

Keep the tube with the scope chart, the docked Coming up and the lit To do rail. Equalise the dock row heights, lighten the left sidebar on Status and Plans, and move Finish setting up back to a prominent place for a new install.
Keep the head-to-box rail and the amber 'was due' stamps. Replace the full-width glowing Add bar on To do with a narrower key, and re-centre the rail lamp on the question line without hand-tuning.
Keep the serif and slate system and the Chat rail. Add the head-to-box rail and the stamped overdue wording from its child so Home also carries the line language.

Keep the lit question and the boxed controls with their lit ticks. Extend the rail to To do and Home lists so the line language runs across pages, and pull the Status, Plans and Settings pages away from plain white-on-black by adding the tube light or a lit rule.
Keep the condensed display type and the numbered index. Swap cream and brass for cool bone and steel, and add tracks or rails to the lists so the page has the owner's line art.

judges.notes: The owner's strongest signals are fine line art that draws structure through every page, glow kept where the phosphor is, and grounded companion colour. The Grid Console pair does this best: tracks, nodes and a lit NOW line run through Home, To do, Plans, Status and Settings while bright green is saved for the key word, the monitors and the primary key. Calmer is the better of the two because the lattice no longer competes with the glow. Desk Terminal is the boldest and most CRT-like, but also the busiest. Track Diagram is the most tasteful and calm, with good rails. Lit Index has the best typesetting, but the least line language, and the owner has asked for that language specifically. Every finalist is clearly different from today across the page content, not only a corner. Note: the scores array contains one stray placeholder row with id r19-mut-4-ref-skip, which is not a design and should be ignored.

parts.what: Lit NOW node on a vertical rail, amber dots for overdue tasks with 'N days ago' timetable margin
Section heads set into a thin tracked rule with a node, calmer steel-edged cells without corner ticks
CRT tube with a scanned bar-chart scope and mono readout, docked beside the question
Conversation hung on a rail from Vera's screen to the box, stops for each speaker, times in the margin
Condensed display headlines with numbered index labels and mono small caps
44px target system, boxed checkboxes and selects with lit ticks, one quiet outline weight

scores.why: Today's page is lit and alive, with a haloed key word, a real tube and radar and a faint scanline. It is also nearly monochrome, flat on the rest of the page, and the Matrix association comes from there.

The most phosphor of the field. Vera's question is typed on a lit scanlined screen, Next up holds a dot-scope, Ideas a radar with numbered blips and Status a swept dial gauge. It is the green screen made into the page's content, not a corner, with grounded slate and amber around it and a lit rail down To do. Risks: the dock row has uneven heights and Finish setting up is buried.

The scanlined, haloed MIND is the strongest single phosphor moment in the field, and the steel-bezel tube carries the radar well. The cool bone and steel are grounded and make the glow read against them. The rail chat adds a lit node. The condensed poster type is bold, and the dim '?' is mismatched.

Same lit scanlined MIND and a tube with a warm cream bezel. Hatched kind swatches and ruled indexes give the page material beyond the green. It is slightly less cool and cohesive than Cool Rail, but the cream and brass have more character.

A teal-lit lattice with a glowing rail and NOW node gives a console feel across the whole page, and the tube and radar are good. The poster question's light is split between pale grey and green, so the soul is more 'instrument panel' than green screen, and the tube is the only deep phosphor.

Same console with the corner ticks removed and a quieter poster, so there is less lit identity. Calmer and tidier, with 44px targets, but the afterglow of the grid is partly traded away. The difference from its parent is small.

Coarser scanlines in the key word and a rail ending in a lit lamp are nice touches. The serif cream headings and slate page are grounded but move away from CRT feel, and the soul sits in the Home head and the tube.
Serif cream headings and a calm slate page with a glowing key word and tube. Tasteful, but the least phosphor in the field. The light is confined to the greeting box, the key word and the monitor.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the typed question on the lit screen, the scope and gauge instruments and the rail down To do. Equalise the dock row heights, and put Finish setting up back above To do on a fresh install.

Keep the scanlined, haloed MIND and the cool bone and steel. Lift the '?' to match MIND, add a small phosphor touch to the rail chat nodes, and carry the screen-lit treatment onto the Plans and To do rows.
Keep the lit MIND, the warm bezel and the hatched swatches. Move toward the cooler steel neutrals of Cool Rail for the bezel and plates, and add a glowing node to the list heads.
Keep the lit rail, the NOW node and the console tube. Reduce the teal wash on the lattice and put the poster question fully in phosphor, so the light has one source.
Keep the 44px targets and baseline heads. Bring back one lit marker per cell (the corner tick on hover only) and restore the poster's key word to full glow, so calm does not become lifeless.
Keep the coarse scanlines in the key word and the rail to the lamp. Set the headings in a face with phosphor character, or glow the count numerals, so the head is not all cream serif.
Keep the quiet slate and the haloed tube. Spread the phosphor beyond the greeting card: lit list designators, scanlined count figures and a screen-lit track.

judges.notes: The two designs that make the green screen the substance of the page, Docked Track with its typed question, scopes and gauge and the Lit Index family with its scanlined poster MIND, clearly lead on soul. Grid Console is lit, but by a teal lattice more than a tube. The Track Diagram pair is the most tasteful and the least CRT. Cool Rail is a good refinement of Lit Index. Docked Track is richest and most visibly different from today across pages, Home, Ideas, Status and Chat alike.

parts.what: Vera's question typed in mono on a lit scanlined screen with a LISTENING status line
Scanlined, haloed poster key word MIND with a bright #6dff9c band
Dot-scope bar chart, numbered-blip radar and swept dial gauge on the tubes
Lit rail with NOW node and amber dots on overdue tasks
Cool bone and steel ink on slate plates with lilac and amber companions
Thread hung on a steel rail with margin times and lit ring at the composer

scores.why: Fine green-on-black base with real CRT halo. Every page is the same rounded dark cards with a green wash, so there is little point of view beyond the tube, and it still reads a bit Matrix.

The most memorable identity. A poster-scale condensed WHAT'S ON YOUR MIND? with a scanlined lit key word, big numbered indexes and ruled colour tabs, and the green screen's light back where attention belongs. The new rail chat and cool bone/steel palette make it feel grounded. Risk: the dim ? beside the bright MIND, and the list pages are mostly type rather than new structure.

The most inventive structure. Each page gets a docked instrument tube with a contents plate, ledger rows with leaders, and a lit track down To do. It is a coherent system and the light stays on the glass. It is a bit dense and busy at the top, and the dock rows are uneven.

Serif heads with lit counts, the gauge and the rail from Vera's screen to the question box give it a warm, literate, instrument-panel mood that looks different from the others. The wide neon Add key on To do glares, and the rail is thin.
Bold lit-index poster typography with heavy condensed titles and strong scanlined light. The warm cream and brass is less grounded than its cool successor, and the chat is plainer without the rail.

Calmer grid console with a good baseline-aligned head and a NOW-lit track. The lattice, cell borders and boxes feel like a generic HUD, and the poster question is quieter, so the difference from its parent is small.
Elegant serif and rail character with a good chat timeline. It is close to mut-2, which refines it, so it adds nothing new here.
Full lattice with corner ticks and hatched plates is the busiest and most gimmicky. The lit track is nice, but the grid noise competes with the content.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster MIND, rail chat and cool slate plates. Raise the ? to match MIND's brightness. Bring the lists closer to Home with a few lit numerals or tray structure so Status, To do and Settings are not just big titles.
Keep the docked tube and contents plate and the ledger rows. Equalise the dock row heights. Put Finish setting up back up top on a fresh install. Thin the chrome so the page does not feel crowded.
Keep the serif heads, the rail to the box and the amber 'was due' stamps. Tone the full-width Add key down to a normal-width key. Thicken the rail slightly.
Keep the poster type and ruled index. Cool the cream and brass to slate and bone, and add the chat rail, as its child did.
Keep the 44px target system, the baseline heads and the NOW track. Give the cells one signature material or edge so the grid reads as more than a HUD.
Superseded by mut-2. Keep its serif heads and rail chat, and fold in the was-due stamps.
Keep the lit track and NOW node. Remove the lattice background, corner ticks and hatching, as mut-4 began to do.

judges.notes: The finalists split into three characters: the poster Lit Index (head-2 and mut-3), the instrument-and-ledger Desk Terminal (mut-1), and the serif rail families (Track Diagram and Grid Console). Lit Index wins on identity. Its big scanlined lit key word brings back the original tube's unique effect while the cool slate keeps everything else grounded. Desk Terminal is the most structurally fresh and the best system for pages beyond the sheets. Track Diagram is the loveliest in tone. Grid Console is the most generic. All of them are visibly different from today across every page, not just in a corner.

parts.what: Poster-scale condensed question with a bright scanlined lit key word and a numbered index title
Terminal Vera card, with a bar-chart tube and an ON THIS PAGE contents plate docked under it
Ledger rows with leaders and a lit rail with branches, plus amber 'was due N days' stamps
Heavy condensed display titles paired with a mono small-caps label and a clean sans body
Thread hung on a steel rail with margin times and a lit ring where the composer begins
Lit NOW node on a track, with amber overdue dots and a late count

scores.why: A coherent single-colour system with a real halo, but ink and green are uniformly bright, and hierarchy and grounding are thin. It is the yardstick for the 'too bright, too contrasty' complaint.

The strongest system. One pattern repeats on every page: a left monitor pillar with a contents plate and a status lamp, a plain-spoken head, slate plates and a bright key only where it matters. The glow stays inside the tubes, so light is where attention belongs. Targets are 0 under 44px, the phone Send is a full key, the focus rings are consistent, and the lit rail on To do ties state to rows. The change is visible across every page, not in a corner.

The most distinctive type system: condensed display, mono labels, numbered designators and double rules that would hold on any page. The scanlined MIND is the best return of the original tube light. Boxed controls with a lit tick are a good system fix. Settings and Status are crisp and Plans is clean. The cost is that To do and Home below the fold are sparse and poster-sized, and the huge MIND is the brightest thing in the field.

A calmer lattice, a 44px target token and baseline-aligned heads make this the most disciplined engineering. The lit track gives a coherent spine on To do, Settings, Ideas and Status. Pages read as one console and cells are tidy. It is still busy: ruled rails, grid floor and panels everywhere, and the differences from the r18 parent are quiet.

The serif display heads pair warmly with sans and mono, and the amber 'was due' stamps and the rail to the box are good ideas. Cards inside cards give heavy chrome. The full-width bright Add key on To do is glare and breaks the 'bright only where needed' rule. The Home rail is hand-tuned and thin.
A sound console system with a lit track and NOW node, but busy grid chrome, small mono labels and many 20px targets. Superseded by mut-4's calmer, 44px version.
A strong poster type system, but plain default controls, a dim chat and a harsh dotted leader. Mut-3 fixes these, so the parent is the weaker form of the same idea.
Good rail concept and grounded slate, but it is the base for mut-2 with fewer fixes. The overdue state is shown only by dot colour, controls are heavy chips, and the To do list is less legible.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the pillar, the docked Coming up row, the big phone Send and the To do rail. Equalise the dock row heights (the 50px gap) and restore Finish setting up to the top for a fresh install. Make the Ideas filter banks wrap instead of scrolling.

Keep the type system, the boxed tick controls and the scanlined MIND. Tighten the vertical rhythm on To do and Home below the fold, where the poster heads leave too much dead space. Pull the MIND brightness down a notch and bring the ? up to match.

Keep the --hit token, the baseline heads and the calmer cells. Reduce the number of simultaneous rails and glows (the floor grid and the footer 'UP' lamp). Give the lit-corner identity back to one element, such as the focused cell.
Keep the serif heads, the amber 'was due' stamps and the Home rail. Shrink the Add key to a normal primary size. Flatten the nested cards on Settings and To do, and make the rail thicker.
Adopt the mut-4 calming and the 44px token. Keep the NOW node and the lit track.
Take the mut-3 boxed controls and the chat rail. Replace the dotted leaders with short rules.
Take mut-2's written 'was due' stamp. Replace the dot-chip filters with a compact segmented control.

judges.notes: The two leaders differ in kind. Mut-1 is a dense, usable app that repeats one pillar pattern on every page. Mut-3 is an editorial type system with the strongest recovery of the tube's scanlines and halo. I put mut-1 first because the light stays inside the monitors, the page is calmer and more grounded, and phone use is better. Mut-3 is close behind and has the better type. All seven fix the 'nearly identical' complaint more than today's page does, because the change shows across the content of every page. The r18 comparators lose to their own improved descendants.

parts.what: The Home tube and Vera card: typed question in a monitor with a listening lamp, and the docked monitor with chart and contents plate
Condensed display heads with numbered designators and mono small-cap labels, on a double rule
The scanlined gradient key word with its halo, with #6dff9c held only on the lit part
Boxed checkbox with a lit tick, a select with a caret cell, and a double-ring focus
The lit track with a NOW node and amber late dots down the To do rows
To do rows with a lit rail and 'was due N days ago' in amber, a facts column and a bigger row type

scores.why: Clear and familiar, but the stock Home is a mass of equally glowing boxes. Two targets sit under 44px on Home (45 under on the full count), and the bar is dense.

Sight line is the best of the field: small label, then the lit MIND, then the one full-width Send, then content. Squinted, the word is the unmistakable anchor. Boxed controls with a lit tick, 44px nav and the chat hung on a rail with times in the margin make state and next step easy to read. Weak spots: the dim '?' looks unmatched, and the phone head change is subtle.

Zero targets under 44px and the phone has a big Send key. The Contents plate, the 'was due N days ago' stamps and the tabular Ideas rows (drive, for, #) let someone find things quickly. The question is a small terminal line, so the squinted hierarchy is softer than the posters. The Ideas filter column wraps into many rows, and Finish setting up has dropped down the page.

Every target reaches 44px and the lattice is calmer. The NOW node on a lit line gives a clear time anchor and baseline-aligned heads read well. The poster question works but sits in a modest box. The phone Send is an icon only, and the difference from the parent is quiet.

The poster question and big indexed section heads are very scannable, and Send is wide on the phone. The controls are less boxed, so state is less obvious. Compared with r19-mut-3 it has no rail chat and weaker control affordance.
The grid gives a consistent module structure and the NOW line works. About 20 Home targets are under 44px and the lattice chrome is busy, so the eye has more to filter before it finds the one action.

The rail down the chat and the To do track are good ideas, and the keyword works as the focal point on the phone. It is close to today's page structurally, with only 1 target under 44px. The phone box is still crowded.

The rail from Vera to the box and the amber 'was due' text are good. On the phone the box is indented, the select wraps to two lines ('who is / asking?') and the textarea clips its placeholder. That is a real usability regression, and it is otherwise nearly the same as r18-mut-3.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the bright MIND, boxed controls and rail chat. Brighten or match the '?' to MIND. Shorten the dotted leader on the rail so it stays close to short lines, and make the phone head change more visible.

Keep the big phone Send, the tabular rows and the 'was due' stamps. Equalise the dock row heights, return Finish setting up to the top on a fresh install, and give the question more weight than a small terminal line so it wins when squinted.
Keep the 44px system (--hit) and the baseline heads. Put back some lit-corner identity on active cells only, and give the phone Send a word as well as an icon.
Keep the poster question and the indexed heads. Take the boxed controls, the 44px nav and the rail chat from r19-mut-3. Make the select state clearer.
Take the calmer lattice and 44px targets from r19-mut-4. Keep the NOW line.
Keep the rail and the lit key word. Make the phone head tighter, and use r19-mut-2's 'was due N days ago' wording.
Fix the phone composer first: do not indent the box, keep the select on one line, show the full textarea placeholder. Keep the rail to the box and the 'was due N days ago' wording.

judges.notes: The Lit Index family wins on glance comprehension: the poster question and big section heads survive squinting, and the one action is obvious. r19-mut-3 adds the control affordances (boxed checkbox, select with a caret cell, 44px nav) and the rail chat, so it takes first place. r19-mut-1 is the most useful page for finding things: contents plate, tabular rows, 'was due' stamps, zero small targets. It is slightly less striking when squinted. Grid Console is coherent but its chrome competes with the content. Rail Keys has a phone composer regression (wrapped select, clipped placeholder).

parts.what: Lit poster question with a bright gradient MIND over a small label and the single full-width Send
Terminal question line with a LISTENING status bar and level ticks inside Vera's card
Tabular rows with designator, facts columns and 'was due N days ago' stamps along a lit track
NOW node with a time readout on the lit line; amber overdue dots
Boxed checkbox with a lit tick, select with a caret cell, 44px nav targets
Thread hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark, times in the left margin, lit ring at the composer

scores.why: A single rounded sans with one big bold title and mono micro-labels. It is clean and legible, but the hierarchy is flat and the scale has few steps. Home's question is the same size as the body, and nothing sets the figures.

The most complete type system. A condensed grotesque poster face, tracked mono caps for labels, a plain sans for body, and numbered running heads. The chat thread sets times in the margin and puts speaker labels in mono caps. The day numerals and the 'IN 6 DAYS' tags are well set. The brighter MIND gives a real focal point, though the dim '?' beside it is a small mismatch. Cool bone is easier on the eye than cream.

The same excellent face pairing and index numbering as r19-mut-3: poster scale, mono caps and clear section rhythm. The cream and brass warmth suits the display face, but the chat is a plain log with no margin times, and the controls are weaker. It is slightly less refined than its child.

The best list typesetting: leader dots, right-aligned tabular columns, small-cap column heads, and amber 'was due' set inline. It also has a good mono readout and gauge lettering. The Desk Terminal's mono question line is characterful, but the faces are plainer, the hierarchy flatter and the page denser than the poster systems. Ideas row text at 19px reads well.

The condensed display face with mono caps is a good pairing. Its real typographic fix is title, count and deck on one last baseline, which is a careful typesetter's improvement. The lowered lead words let the key word lead. The 44px targets cost nothing visually. The changes are quiet at half size.

The same type system as mut-4, with the title, count and deck baselines not yet aligned. The poster lead words compete with the lit key word. The tracked mono labels are well set, but the headings feel cramped against the lattice.

The serif display with a tabular underlined count (Ideas 12, Status 6) is the most elegant heading treatment, and it pairs well with the sans and mono. Home's question is small, though, and the coarser scanlines make 'mind' slightly harder to read. The stacked 'was due N days ago' stamp is fussy at small size.

The same handsome serif-and-sans pairing and counted heads as mut-2, but Home's question is modest and the hierarchy is soft. The 'Vera asks' line in the chat is a nice touch. The type is very close to its child, with nothing new to add.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the type system and the margin-time thread. Fix the dim '?' by giving it the same lit gradient at a lower stop. Keep the phone question from dropping below two clear lines. Use tabular figures wherever the counts stack.
Keep the poster and index system. Take r19-mut-3's rail thread and margin times for the chat, and its brighter key word, so the display face has a lit anchor.

Keep the leaders and tabular columns. Pair the mono question with a stronger display step for page titles. Equalise the dock row heights so the left column does not leave a gap. Keep column-head small caps at one tracking value across pages.
Keep the last-baseline heads. Restore a strong, lit scale step for the Home question and make the mono labels less uniformly tracked across the pages.
Adopt mut-4's baseline alignment. Keep the tracked mono labels. Add room around the section heads so they do not sit tight against the lattice rules.

Keep the serif count heads. Enlarge the Home question to match its serif titles. Return the key word's scanline pitch to a legible one. Set 'was due' on one line in small caps instead of a stacked stamp.
Keep the serif and tabular count heads. Raise Home's question to a clear display step so the hierarchy has a top, and use one numeral style for all counts.

judges.notes: The poster-grotesque systems (r19-mut-3, r18-head-2) lead on typesetting. They have a real scale, with a display face at poster size, tracked mono caps for labels, and tabular day numerals. They also change every page visibly, which answers the owner's complaint. r19-mut-3 adds the margin-time thread and a brighter key word, so it edges ahead. Desk Terminal has the best row and column setting but a flatter hierarchy. The Grid pair is well set, and mut-4's shared baseline is a small, real fix. The serif pairing is elegant but gives Home too little display weight. Today's page is legible but undifferentiated.

parts.what: Condensed grotesque display, tracked mono-caps labels, plain sans body, numbered running heads
Title, count and deck on one last baseline; serif title with tabular underlined count as the alternative
Rows with leader dots and right-aligned tabular facts columns, with small-cap column heads
Steel-rail thread with times set in the left margin and mono-caps speaker labels
Mono readout with a gauge dial and a labelled bar trace on the tubes
Brighter scanlined key word with a layered halo as the one lit focal point

scores.why: Clear and familiar, with a labelled bottom bar and a simple Settings grid. The phone composer is cramped (Send sits alone on a row), the To do rows are small, and the Home targets include 45 under 44px.

Easiest to use. The phone Send is a full key with its word, the composer is tall, and every Home target is 44px or more. The desktop 'On this page' contents plate and Ready line show state at a glance. To do has a bright 'Add a task' key, 'was due 6 days ago' in amber, pill filters and a lit track. Cost: the left tube column is heavy on Settings, and Finish setting up moved down.

Calmer grid and every target at 44px (none under on Home). To do has the best state cues: due dates in a column and a NOW node on the track. Plans cells are clear. The grid is still busy for tired eyes, the Add something to do disclosure is easy to miss, and the Filter select is small.

Clean phone composer on one row (select, mic, Send). Plans has a clock and clear plan chips, and To do has Open/Done/Cancelled/All pill filters. The late dates are bare dots with a date, and 'Add something to do' is a plain collapsed row, so the primary action is weak.

Full-width SEND and boxed controls are very clear, and the nav is 44px. Big poster headings help scanning. They also push the box down on the phone and make Settings wide and sparse. The tiny mono tab labels (00 HOME) and 9px kicker text are hard to read at night.

Best primary Add key on To do and 'was due N days ago' is plain language. But the phone Home composer is broken: the textarea is clipped so the placeholder cuts off, and 'who is asking?' wraps to two lines in the select. Home is the family's first task, so this costs a lot.

Strong hierarchy and a big Send. The condensed poster type takes much of the screen and makes Settings and To do spacious but slow to scan. The mono caps nav and kickers are small, and the unboxed controls are less obviously clickable.

The tracked To do and the gauge are informative. The lattice, corner ticks and hatched plates make a noisy page. 20 Home targets are under 44px and the status line is cramped, so it is worse on a phone at night than its calmer child.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the big Send, the one-row filters and the amber was-due rows. Equalise the dock row heights, put Finish setting up back near the top on a fresh install, and shrink the tube column on Settings so the list gets more width.
Keep the 44px token and the NOW track. Make 'Add something to do' a visible key, since a collapsed row hides the main action. Replace the small Filter select with pills, and lift the dim ink-2 text.
Keep the clean one-row composer and the pill filters. Promote Add something to do to a bright key and write 'was due N days ago' beside the amber dots, as r19-mut-2 does. Raise the 9px mono labels.

Keep the boxed checkbox and select and the full-width SEND. Shrink the poster question on the phone so the box is reachable sooner. Raise the tiny mono tab labels and kickers, and make the ? as bright as MIND.

Keep the wide Add key and the was-due wording. Remove the 34px indent in the Home box so the select does not wrap and the textarea shows its full placeholder. Lock the rail lamp to the box with CSS, not a hand-tuned offset.
Keep the Send key and the clear section order. Reduce the poster scale on Settings and To do rows, replace the mono nav with plain 44px labels, and box the controls.
Keep the gauge and the tracked To do. Drop the lattice, ticks and hatched plates (mut-4 did) and bring every target to 44px.

judges.notes: The usability differences are fine. r19-mut-1 wins because it makes the first tasks easiest (a big labelled Send, a tall composer, 44px targets, a page contents plate, a visible primary Add key, was-due wording and pill filters) and still differs from today's page across every page. The Grid Console Calmer comes next for its 44px targets and the best state cues in To do. The Lit Index poster designs read well but cost screen space and use tiny mono labels. r19-mut-2's clipped phone composer is a real task-breaking defect on the most-used screen. Nothing was removed that the family needs. The Home squinted view still shows Send and the box as the brightest elements in most designs.

parts.what: Title with the page's one bright primary key beside it (Add a task / Add a plan), plus a short deck and a count
Tube with a status line, docked over an 'On this page' contents plate and a Ready readout
To do rows with a lit track, amber 'was due N days ago' and the owner and a pencil on the right
Full-width labelled Send with a tall composer on the phone, pill filters in place of selects, boxed checkboxes
Lit NOW node on the To do track with the due date column, amber for late
Plans clock and week key; the spend gauge on Status

scores.why: Yardstick. Bright green on black everywhere with one soft bloom, so it is monochrome and tiring. The glow is carried by every green thing rather than by the few that matter. It does keep the original tube effect, which several finalists have lost.

Changes the page's content structure: Home now has a Coming up band, a Contents plate and a tube with typed glowing text. Each list page gets its own machine (gauge, chart, readout), and the To do rows get a lit rail. It brings back the most tube light and keeps the slate ground and amber 'was due'. Faults: the dock row is uneven, Finish setting up is demoted, and the pages carry a lot of plates.

The boldest typesetting and the most visible change on every page. Poster condensed titles under colour-coded rules, a scanlined MIND with halo, a rail thread in Chat, and boxed controls with a lit tick. Cool bone and steel avoid the brass wash. Faults: the huge MIND edges toward glare, the list pages are sparse text on black with little phosphor, and the dim '?' looks orphaned.

The grid, floor, bloom and tubes give the strongest ambient CRT light, and a 44px target system is a real gain. Calming the lattice is sensible. But it is nearly identical to its parent at half size, the ground reads greenish, and the grid is close to the Matrix or console costume.

The Home rail from Vera's screen to the box is a nice idea, and the amber 'was due N days ago' is plain and useful. But it is a thin delta on r18-mut-3. The full-width bright Add key on To do is glare, and the serif plus cream feels like an editor theme.

A coherent console with a strong phosphor feel and a good NOW track. It is busy, with hatched dead plates and corner ticks, and the green-tinted ground is a wash. It is the parent of mut-4, which fixes some of this.

Distinct editorial poster type and good hierarchy. The Matrix risk is gone, but the lists are flat, the cream and brass is slightly bronze, and the chat is plain. Its child r19-mut-3 improves it on nearly every count.

Calm, grounded and well structured, with a scanlined key word and a rail. Its serif titles and cream read as a different product, and the tube light is thin outside the monitors. It is the base of mut-2, which only adds a little to it.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the dock row, the glowing terminal question and the tracked To do rows. Equalise the heights of Coming up and the Contents plate. Put Finish setting up back above the fold when the install is fresh. Thin the plate count on Status.

Keep the poster type, the rail chat and the boxed controls. Dim the MIND lead a step and give the '?' the same scanlines. Bring tube glow and a lit marker to the To do and Settings rows so they are not flat.

Keep the 44px token and the baseline heads. Neutralise the green tint of the ground. Make the cells and plates visibly different in the lists, not only in a few steps of grey. Cut the floor grid to one place.

Keep the Home rail with its lamp and the plain amber 'was due' stamp. Shrink the Add key to a normal size, or make it a keycap in the head rather than a full-width bar. Recover the tube feel the serif titles took away.
Keep the Now track and the console shell. Remove the hatched dead plates and the lit corner ticks, and take the green tint out of the ground.
Keep the poster titles and the numbered index. Swap cream and brass for the cool bone and steel. Give the lists row-level glow and a thread for the chat.
Keep the scanlined key word and the rail. Swap the serif for a sturdier face, and add a stronger tube light and structural difference on Home and Ideas.

judges.notes: The owner's test is whether the difference reaches the page content. r19-mut-1 passes it best, because the Home layout, the machine on every page and the To do rail all change. It also restores real tube light in the question, the gauge and the readouts. r19-mut-3 is second: its typesetting is the most visible change across all pages. r19-mut-4 and r18-head-5 have the lushest CRT atmosphere, but that atmosphere is a green wash and the grid risks costume. r19-mut-2 and r18-mut-3 are near-duplicates, and their warm serif look is the least phosphor of the set. Every finalist except r19-mut-1 keeps most of its list pages as flat text on black, so the lists are where the next round should spend its effort.

parts.what: Terminal tube with a glowing typed question, a listening status line and the Contents plate docked beside it
Larger rows with leader dots, a facts column and a lit rail with a branch to each tick, ending at a NOW node
Condensed poster titles with mono caps labels and a scanlined key word
Amber 'was due N days ago' stamp on a rail with a lit NOW lamp
Framed checkbox that lights and holds a tick, a select with a caret cell, and a tall Send key on the phone
Thread hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark, with times in the left margin and a lit ring at the composer

scores.why: Keeps the glow and tube, but it is a wash of green on black with little variation, the very thing the owner asked to change.
Grounded slate with a real tube and a typed question, and the change shows across Home, Chat and Ideas. The lists are plain text rows with little line art, and the left column of Home ends in a void.
Signal Box's line language carried through Home, To do, Chat and Ideas, over slate with amber, cyan and a little violet. The tube keeps its glow and scanlines, and the page is calm.

A bold poster-type redesign that is unmistakably different, but the giant lit MIND is the brightest, most contrasty thing on any card, and the hatched orange, blue and green swatches drift from the CRT feel.
A console grid with lit rails, a NOW node and a To do timetable, which is the line art the owner loves, with real tube glow. The corner ticks and hatched blank plates add clutter.

Fixes the void in Desk Terminal's left column by docking Coming up and Contents under the tube, and adds a lit rail on To do. It is solid and grounded, but still the plainest list treatment of the field.

The rail from Vera's screen to the question box draws the eye through the page, and the 'was due N days ago' stamps and wide Add key give the content a clearer voice. Grounded colour, glowing key word with coarse scanlines, and the Signal Box lines carried through.
The chat hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark is lovely and the cool bone and steel suit the green. The poster MIND is still the loudest item on the page, and its look is far from the CRT original.

The best-calmed console: line art, lit track, NOW node and 44px targets, with the clutter of corner ticks and hatching removed. It keeps the tube glow where the phosphor is and is modern, grounded and still a CRT. The change is quiet at half size.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the calmed lattice, lit track and 44px system. Bring back one small lit signature on each cell (a top-edge highlight or a glowing corner dot) so the Grid keeps its console identity, and add the Home rail from Vera's screen to the box (from r19-mut-2).

Keep the rail from Vera's screen to the question box, the amber 'was due' stamps and the coarse scanlines in the key word. Make the rail thicker or add a node mid-way so it reads at half size, and give the greeting back the width it took from Next up so the tube does not wrap.
Keep the dock row and the lit rail on To do. Equalise the heights of Coming up and Contents. Borrow the Signal Box tracks and the amber stamps so the list rows stop reading as plain text.

Lift the rail chat thread and the cool bone and steel palette into a design with a calmer head. Tone the giant MIND down: lower the brightness, narrow the fill, and keep the halo and scanlines instead of a bright slab.
The poster type is a bold idea, but the lit word needs to sit lower in brightness. Replace the hatched orange, blue and green swatches with cyan or slate line icons.

judges.notes: The Signal Box family (Track Diagram, Grid Console) is where the owner's praise sits: thin lines that delimit areas and lead the eye, over grounded slate, with the tube glowing where the phosphor is. Of the two new entries in that family, Grid Console Calmer and Rail Keys are real, if modest, improvements on their parents. Desk Terminal is grounded and the best on the monitor (waveform, typed question, grid floor), but its lists are the plainest. Lit Index is the biggest visible change across every page, but it is also the brightest and most contrasty, and it is furthest from the CRT soul. It is worth developing only with calmer lit type. The yardstick (today) is clearly the least varied card.

parts.what: Vera's lit screen with a steel rail turning to the question box and ending at a lit lamp
To do on a vertical lit track with a 'now' node, amber 'was due' ladder at left and a DUE timetable margin
Thread hung on a steel rail from Vera's mark, times in the margin, a lit ring where the box begins
Green-black slate plates with amber for late, soft cyan and violet for kinds, and the bright green held back for the lit things
Condensed poster headings with a mono label scale and numbered running heads (runner-up: serif section heads with a lit numeral)
Key word with coarse scanlines and layered halo, the tube's bloom, and a grid floor in the monitor

scores.why: The yardstick: the key-word halo, one monitor and the glowing dots are all there, but the rest of the page is plain dark cards with little tube light, so only the corner and a few marks feel like a green screen.

The phosphor reaches across the pages: Vera's question is typed on a real tube with a LISTENING line, Status has a dial in a bezel, Ideas has a radar, and the Home chart has a perspective floor. Light stays on the glass and the surrounding page is grounded.

Same strongest tube set as r18-mut-1, plus Coming up docked under the glass and a lit rail down the To do rows, which carries the afterglow into the list. It is the most phosphor across content, with calm elsewhere.
One good scanlined key word and a bezelled radar monitor, but the cream serif heads and slate plates make the rest of the page quiet, so the tube is a lone island.

The rail from Vera's lit screen to a lamp at the question, and the coarser scanlines in the key word, add true light in the content. The cream serif and slate still make the page calm to the point of a little lifeless.

A giant scanlined MIND with a halo is the most striking lit word, and the beige-bezel monitor is period-true. But the poster type is more editorial than green screen, and Ideas and Status are mostly cream and hatched with little tube light.

Brightens and scanlines the poster key word to full phosphor and cools the bezel and neutrals, so the lit effect is stronger against slate. Rail and boxed ticks add small lit details. Still a lone big word, with a mismatched dim question mark.
A lit lattice, a NOW node, glowing track lines and a monitor with a grid floor give a console feel. The bright MIND is cropped and many outlined cells flatten the glow.

Calms the lattice and quiets the lead words so the key word and rail carry the light, which is tasteful. But it removes lit corner ticks, so it gives up some of the console glow, and the poster looks like the parent.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the tube set (typed question, dial, radar, chart) and the lit To do rail. Equalise the dock row so Coming up and the Contents plate end together, and bring Finish setting up back near the top on a fresh install.
Kept as the baseline. Its tubes are the strongest, but the dock gap and the blank column under Coming up are what r19-mut-1 fixes.
Keep the brighter, scanlined poster key word and the cool bezel. Brighten or scanline the question mark so it matches MIND, and carry a tube (dial or radar) onto Status so the light is not one word.

Keep the head-to-box rail with its lamp and the coarse-scanline key word. Anchor the lamp to the question line so a wrapped line cannot leave it off, and give the Status and Ideas heads a lit element so the glow is not confined to Home.
Keep the calmer lattice and the 44px targets. Put back one lit feature per cell, such as a glowing top edge on hover or active, so the console has light and not only line.

judges.notes: The Desk Terminal line wins on soul because the green screens carry the page content: the typed question with its LISTENING status, the dial, the radar and the chart each sit in a real bezel, and the light stays on the glass while the page around them is grounded. That meets the owner's request for the original's tube effect without going back to a green wash. The Lit Index (r19-mut-3) has the single strongest lit word, a scanlined, haloed MIND, but its light is confined to that word and the Ideas and Status heads are cream and hatched. The Track Diagram (r19-mut-2) has a good idea in the rail and lamp, but its cream serif and slate are very calm. The Grid Console (r19-mut-4) shows good discipline in calming the lattice. Its lit key word is half-cropped, and calming it removed some console glow. The differences between r19-mut-1 and r18-mut-1 are small and mostly lower on the page, which my cards show only partly. The r19 mutations are mostly modest changes to their parents, so the real contest is between the families, and Desk Terminal leads.

parts.what: Key word as a bright #6dff9c gradient with scanlines and a strong halo, so the poster word is the lit centrepiece
Vera's question typed in glyph type with a block cursor on a tube, with a LISTENING status line, plus a docked Contents plate and status under the tube
Poster question with a bright scanlined key word and a bone head; or the baseline-aligned title, count and deck line
Steel rail from Vera's lit screen to a lit lamp at the question box; the glowing live dot and NOW node on the track
Spend dial in a bezelled tube (needle, tick scale, LIMIT flag), plus the radar and the chart with a lit floor grid

scores.why: Lovely halo and tube, but a sea of near-identical green-glowing cards with one voice and no typographic personality; this is the 'Matrix' the family named.
Terminal with a typed question, a status line and a contents plate is tidy and grounded, but it reads as a well-made dashboard; the type is one voice and the identity is polite.
Docking Coming up under the card fixes the void and the lit rail on To do is a nice touch, but it is the same dashboard with the same sans and little new mood.
A serif display face for Vera and the lilac Ideas numeral, with a steel rail and lit nodes down the chat, give an editorial, instrument-panel feel unlike any stock dark theme.
Adds the rail running from Vera's screen to the question box and the amber 'was due 6 days ago', so the head-to-box path reads as one idea; refined and warmer, though the rail is faint at size.

The poster question in tall condensed type with a scanlined, glowing MIND, the numbered 00-05 index, the colour-coded section bars and hatched kind swatches make a bold, memorable, genuinely new identity, with phosphor light only where it counts.

Keeps the Lit Index poster identity and brightens MIND; the chat hung on a rail from Vera's mark, with margin times and cool bone and steel in place of cream and brass, carries the personality into the conversation. The dim ? beside a brighter MIND is the one flaw.
Condensed headers, numbered cells, a lit track with a NOW node and the grid-floor lamp footer make a coherent control-room language, but the lattice and hatching are busy.
Calming the lattice and aligning head baselines is sensible and tidier, but it loses some console identity and the difference is quiet at half size.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster MIND, the rail chat with margin times and the cool bone and steel. Light the question mark to match MIND, or drop it a step, so the two do not look unmatched, and carry the poster headings and rail down to Plans, To do and Settings.
Keep the index nav and the colour-coded section bars as the system. Fix the dim question mark, and give the chat the rail thread so the conversation is as designed as Home.
The rail from Vera's screen to the box is the best new idea here. Thicken it and let it glow a little so it shows at half size, and anchor the lamp to the box by layout, not a hand-tuned offset.
Keep the lit track, the NOW node and the condensed heads. Thin the lattice and hatched plates (as Calmer began to) but keep one lit corner mark per cell so it still reads as a console.
Keep the 44px target system and the baseline heads. Restore a little lit-corner identity, in the primary cell only, so calm does not become plain.

judges.notes: The two Lit Index entries stand out: a poster-scale scanlined MIND, a numbered index and colour-coded section bars have a point of view that a family would remember and that nothing generic offers. The Rail and Grid families are coherent and grounded, but they are more dashboard than character. The Desk Terminal pair is competent and the most predictable. All the new designs differ from today across the pages, not just in a corner. The best new ideas are the rail threads (the chat on a rail from her mark, and the rail from the tube to the box). Their weak point is that they are faint at size.

parts.what: Tall condensed poster headings with a mono index and small caps labels; serif display as the alternative voice
Cool bone ink and steel labels on slate plates, with the green kept for light and the hatched kind swatches as the accents
Poster question with a bright scanlined MIND, a listening line and a ruled input
Numbered sections under colour-tipped hairline bars, with a big condensed title and a small count beneath
Typed question on a CRT screen with a LISTENING status line, plus a rail from the tube to the box
Numbered 00-05 index tabs with lettered utilities on the right; a lamp and grid-floor footer as the alternative

scores.why: Coherent and legible, but the whole Home is one green wash with a small Send icon, a cramped starter row and a squinted view where nothing leads; the yardstick.
Tube with typed question, Listening lamp, bars and a grounded slate card give a clear title, then question, then action path; the Send is still a small icon beside the mic.
Real scanlined key word and a good radar monitor, but the composer is cramped and the Next up title wraps to three lines on the phone.
The poster MIND leads the squint test and the Send is a full-width key, so the eye goes title, action, content; the cream/brass tint and glow are a little heavy and the poster eats the first screen.
Grid cells give the Home structure and the poster question reads well with a plain Send icon, but the lattice, corner ticks and violet accents add visual noise and 20 targets are under 44px.
Keeps the best glass and adds a full-width Send with its word and a taller composer, a real phone gain; docking Coming up beside the tube improves the Home but pushes Finish setting up down.
The rail and lamp from Vera's screen to the box is a lovely idea, but the cost is a cramped phone composer: the textarea clips its placeholder and the select wraps to two lines.

Strongest first-screen hierarchy: a bright MIND, a full-width Send and a lit-tick checkbox; cool bone and steel replace the brass and the light is brought back on the key word; 44px nav and boxed controls hold up on a phone at night.
Calmer lattice and every target at 44px (0 under) make it the most usable grid, but the greyed lead words and quiet outlines make it close to its parent at a glance.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the poster question, full Send key, lit-tick boxed controls and the cool palette. Fix the dim '?' next to the bright MIND, and keep the poster to about a third of the phone's first screen so the starters show above the fold.
Keep the big Send with its word and the Vera card with its tube and Listening line. Equalise the dock row's heights, and keep Finish setting up prominent for a fresh install.

Keep the steel rail with its lamp from Vera's screen to the box. On the phone keep the select on one line and the textarea two lines tall, which means giving the rail less indent (about 34px is too much).

Keep the 44px --hit token and the baseline heads. Bring back some lit identity in the cells (one lit edge or an icon tint) so the calm does not read as the old page, and lift the greyed lead words of the question.
The poster is the strongest squint-test lead. Pull the cream back to a cool neutral as in r19-mut-3 and soften the halo on the large letters.

judges.notes: On the use cards, the poster-question designs (Lit Index family) and Desk Terminal with a full Send key lead the eye title, then action, then content most clearly, and the Lit Index family brings back the most tube light on the key word without glare elsewhere. The Grid Console family is the most consistent as a system and r19-mut-4 is the cleanest on targets, but it is the closest to today at half size. The Track Diagram rail is a charming idea that costs phone composer room, which is a real task cost for sending Vera a message. r19-mut-1's big Send and docked Coming up are the best task-oriented changes; r19-mut-3's boxed controls and cool material are the best system-level changes. All designs far exceed today on grounded colour and hierarchy.

parts.what: Boxed controls: lit-tick checkbox frame, select with a caret cell, full-width Send key, 44px nav
Uppercase tab bar of divided 44px cells with a clear lit active cell
Listening lamp and level bars on the tube's status line; a lit lamp where the rail meets the box
Vera card: tube with typed question, tall composer, FROM select, mic and a big Send key, starters below
Poster question with a bright gradient MIND and a running head 'VERA  SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER'

scores.why: Black ground with one green on everything, flat grey cards and bare heads. It is monochrome and the owner calls it too contrasty, though the halo is real.

The tube-and-dial rail on every page is across-the-page content, and the slate case and amber 'was due' are grounded. It has only two or three lit moments and a lot of the same boxed panel, and the sidebar plus tube crowd a narrow page.

Serif display titles with a count, a lit chain down Who answers, a dated timeline with a NOW node and a clock on Plans change all four pages, and the tube keeps the light. The serif could read as editorial or costume in places, but the cream and steel are grounded and the type is clearly the best here.

Heavy condensed titles, indexed numbers and coloured rules change the page structure on every card, and the type is distinctive. It is shouty: Settings is a wall of huge condensed words, and the light is thin (a small tube and a few rules), so the phosphor feeling is mostly gone.

The strongest tube light and glow and a lit trunk through the page, with a clear ledger of cells and a NOW node. Hatched plates, grid lines and cool outlines are busy and edge toward the editor or Matrix-HUD look, and the cell grid feels repeated on every page.

On the lists cards it is a near duplicate of r18-mut-1; the only visible change is a thin green rail on To do rows. The Home dock row is not visible here, so the difference is mostly out of sight and the dock row has an equal-height gap by its own admission.

The Track Diagram parent plus a wide bright Add key, amber 'was due N days ago' and a Plans keycap tray. The full-width glowing green Add bar on To do is glare and out of keeping with the calmer pages, though the plain-spoken overdue stamps are a real gain.

Lit Index with cool bone and steel replacing cream and brass. The lists cards barely differ from the parent apart from a slightly cooler Plans cell, and a boxed select. It is a refinement, not a new idea, and the cool tint is hard to see.

Grid Console with the corner ticks and hatching removed, so the page is calmer and cleaner and the heads sit on one baseline. It answers the clutter I flagged in head-5, but it is the same page as head-5 at half size, and the grid still looks like an editor or HUD.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the serif titles with counts, the lit chain, the timeline and the clock. Make the display serif less cream-heavy (a bit greyer) so it does not read as costume, and add a little more light to the green hairlines.
Keep the amber 'was due N days ago' stamp. Replace the full-width glowing Add bar with a compact right-aligned primary key so the bright green stays a signature, not glare.
Keep the calmer lattice and baseline-aligned heads. Bring back one or two quiet lit marks (the NOW node and trunk) and enlarge the differences from head-5, which are invisible at half size.
Keep the indexed numbers and the coloured rule under each title. Take the title size down one step on Settings, where the condensed type becomes a wall, and let the tube carry more of the light.
Keep the tube, dial and keycap tray. Let the side rail collapse to the tube alone on narrower pages so the content gets its width.

judges.notes: The field is split into four families, and the r19 mutants are mostly small edits on their parents, so several cards are near duplicates. That is exactly what the owner objected to ("those look nearly identical"). The Track Diagram and Grid Console lines do most for the owner's complaint: they change the structure of every page (headers with counts, a timeline with a NOW node, section trunks) and keep real tube light. Lit Index is typographically bold, but it trades light for volume and its r19 cool-rail variant is invisible on these cards. Desk Terminal is solid and grounded, and its r19 docked track adds only a thin rail on the lists pages. Today's page scores low because the single green carries everything.

parts.what: serif display title with a lit-ring icon and a small count and subhead on the same baseline
timeline rows with dated amber pips, the NOW node and a plain 'was due N days ago' stamp
the cost tube with its dial, plus the Plans clock showing the week's past, today and ahead
a lit trunk rail with section heads branching off it, and cells drawn by fill and edge
a vertical lit chain down Who answers, with steel hollow rings for off and amber for needs a look
keycap-tray filters with a lit pip on the held key, and a compact bright Add key
